FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 21 October 1967, after the draft finalized by the Oils and Oilseeds Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council and the Agricultural and Foed Products Division Council. 0.2 The terms' mustard' and' rapeseed' arc frequently used to cover three, more or less similar, seeds of Brassica, fam, Cruciferae, The oleiferous brassicas cultivated in India are divided into three groups, namely (a) Brassica campestris I . inn. (SARSON and TORIA ), (h) Brassica jU11(ea Coss. (RAJ) and (c) Biassica nigra Koch. ( BENARSJ RAJ) which is used only as a spire and not for oil milling. 0.3 Formulation of this standard has been taken up to meet the need felt fer precise and acceptable methods for grading of oilseeds produced and marketed in the country. This standard is based on the trade practices followed in the country in respect of the types and grades of mustard seeds. Mustard seeds covered in this standard are intended for oil milling and IS: 546-1963* corresponds to the oil obtained fiom them. Mustard seeds, either whole or as powder used as spice are not covered in this standard. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2-l960t. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the methods of grading and the requirements for mustard seeds for oil milling, along with relevant methods of sampling and test. �

2. TERMINOLOGY
2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS : 3579.1966: shall apply.
�Specification for mustard oil ("vis,tl). tR.ules for roundinl off numerical valuel ( "vis,tl). :Methods or test for oilleeda.

IS I 4421� 1967

3. TYPBI
3.1 Mustard seeds grown in India shall be grouped into the fonowing three types.

3.1.1 SA.RSON ( B. camjJutru Linn. VII' SARSON) - The seeds are bold, of large size, round in shape and have a smooth surface. They are of three distinct colours: yellow, brown and dark-brown or black. These are generally grown in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Maryana, Bihar, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh.

3.1.2 TORIA or LAB] (B. cam/JIS"ir Linn. va, TOR1A) - The seeds are brown or black in colour. The seeds are slightly smaller than those of S~RSON (I" 3.1.1). The leeds are spherical or ovoid in shape and are reddish or dark-brown in colour. These are generally grown in Punjab, Baryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal. 3.1.3 RAI (B. june,a Coss.) - RAJ seed is generally smaller than SARSON (s" 3.1.1), is black or brown in colour and spherical or ovoid
in shape with a distinctly wrinkled surface.

4. GRADES
4.1 Mustard seeds of the three types shall be graded as follows depending on the requirements prescribed in 5.1: Grade 1, Grade 2 a-id Grade 3.

5. REQ,UlREMENTS
5.1 Mustard seeds of the three types shall be graded in accordance with the physical and chemical requirements given in Table 1.
